approachQuestion.prompt:
Shared Archive Tail

Two nonempty finite acyclic singly linked lists may share a suffix of node objects. Return their first shared object or null if none. Values may repeat and do not define sharing. Do not change links. Only heads are supplied. Let n be the combined lengths, counting a shared node once per traversal, 2 <= n <= 200000.

Input: first A(1) -> C(7) -> D(4), second B(1) -> E(8) -> C -> D, both ending in null. Output: C.
Input: distinct A(5) -> null and B(5) -> null. Output: null.

Choose a method that satisfies the full contract with the best worst-case running time, breaking time ties by least auxiliary storage.

options.text: Copy first-list references into an array. Walk the second list, checking each identity against every array entry; return its first match.
options.feedback: This finds the shared suffix correctly, but repeated scans add avoidable work and storage.

options.text: Align lengths, then return the first pair with equal values.
options.feedback: Distinct A(5) and B(5) have equal values but no shared object.

options.text: Move both heads in lockstep without length alignment, returning a node only if identities meet.
options.feedback: First A -> C -> D and second B -> E -> C -> D never align at their shared nodes.

options.text: Count both lengths, advance the longer list by their difference, then move both references together until identities match or both become null.
options.feedback: Equal remaining lengths align a shared suffix; the first identity match is its first node.

feedback.reason: Equal remaining lengths align a shared suffix; the first identity match is its first node.
details: Count both lengths, advance the longer list by their difference, then move both references together until identities match or both become null.
Shared labels do not prove a shared tail; references must identify the same node. Align remaining path lengths before the tandem walk so both pointers reach an actual shared node at the same step.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (acm-b15-05-target), regardless of your Q1 choice. Here n. Choose the tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Count each node allocation, link access, identity/value comparison and machine-word operation as constant work. Include all temporary collections and call frames; exclude supplied nodes and the final returned output only. Copying or allocating k records costs k operations. No hash-table, amortized-operation or tail-call assumptions are used.
